answer: Escrowed history weighting ties an identity’s voting weight to a slowly maturing record of settled, counterparty-confirmed trades; each new clone starts at the nadir of that curve and must fund real transactions whose escrow is released only after independent counterparties confirm delivery. Because the vine of confirmations grows one edge per completed deal, a farm of clones needs genuinely distinct counterparties, and shared counterparties collapse into one onyx cluster whose weight is capped, so splitting identities yields no extra influence.
